phases.name: Foundation
phases.description: The Product level, written once: what the product is for and how it will be built. Optional, but every epic reads it when it exists.

phases.name: Discover
phases.description: Say what the change is and why: the optional analysis, then the epic.

phases.name: Design
phases.description: Decide how it is built: the architecture and its locked contract, and the user interface when there is one.

phases.name: Plan
phases.description: Split the work into stories, and write the test cases that prove them.

phases.name: Build
phases.description: Each story is built in each repo it names, one lane at a time: spec, tasks, implement and checks by the agent, then a person's engineer review and merge.

steps.name: Foundation
steps.description: Write the Product's foundation once: its purpose, scope, first release (MVP), roadmap, stack, repos and risks. Every epic builds on it.

gate.description: A person reviews the foundation on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Discovery
steps.description: The older product front-zero, replaced by Foundation. Kept so epics that used it still read.

gate.description: A person reviews the discovery on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Analysis
steps.description: Study the problem before the epic: who it is for, the options, and the evidence. The analysis-first and spike routes start here.

gate.description: A person reviews the analysis on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Epic
steps.description: Describe the change: the problem, the goal, what is in and out of scope, and how success is measured. It sets the work-item type the rest of the chain follows.

gate.description: A person reviews the epic on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Architecture
steps.description: Decide how the change is built across the repos, and lock the contract between them. A later change to the locked contract needs its own review.

gate.description: A person reviews the architecture on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: UI design
steps.description: Design the screens and flows, and link the design files. A route may mark it optional, for a change with no user interface.

gate.description: A person reviews the ui design on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Stories
steps.description: Split the epic into stories, each tagged with the repos it touches. Its approval ends Shape, so Build can start.

gate.description: A person reviews the stories on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Test cases
steps.description: Write the test cases that prove the stories work. It runs beside Build, not before it.

gate.description: A person reviews the test cases on its review PR/MR, approves it and merges it. The step moves on only after that merge.

steps.name: Spec
steps.description: For one story in one repo, write the detailed spec the code is built from.

steps.name: Tasks
steps.description: Break the spec into small, ordered tasks, each touching at most 3 files.

steps.name: Implement
steps.description: Write the code and its tests for one task, on the task's branch.

steps.name: Checks
steps.description: Run the CI gates locally, then push and open the PR/MR so CI runs them too.

steps.name: Engineer review
steps.description: A person reviews the PR/MR, approves it and merges it. An AI first pass may help, but the merge is always a person's.
